claims.statement: Build-error overview covers FPT/GHEC/GHES, with Actions-preferred deployment note. Branch pushes may not start builds; absence of an error is not evidence of successful build or deployment.

Unverified-email trigger exclusion is FPT/GHEC conditional; deploy-key pushes and CI source-branch exclusions are separately listed. Machine-user alternative is not authority to create identities or credentials.
Source reports publication can take up to ten minutes; expected delay is not observed success, and missed trigger must be distinguished from queued, failed and completed runs.

Outside build-pages-with-actions scope, Page build warning denotes completed build with potential problems and Page build failed denotes incomplete build. Neither warning status nor complete build establishes effective deployment or application behavior.

Cloud build-pages-with-actions scope directs examining Actions workflow runs and optional reruns. Statement about other CI excluding default build/deploy description must be read alongside publishing-source guide: cloud deployment still uses Actions even when build occurs externally.
Outside Actions-building conditional, repository Settings shows failures but not warnings. Dashboard silence does not establish no warning, no failure or a triggered build.
Local build testing is recommended before pushing to inspect command-line errors. Source recommendation is not a test receipt or guarantee local/hosted version/config parity.

Branch-source PR Checks can expose build errors; custom workflow requires pull_request trigger and recommends skipping deploy steps for PR events. Trigger existence alone does not verify secure event handling, permissions or actual deployment denial.

Branch build failures are described as emailed to primary address subject to GHES mail prerequisite. Notification absence cannot prove success; custom workflow PR trigger instruction alone does not establish recipient notification settings or delivered email.

Third-party CI example Gemfile uses Ruby backticks rather than quoted strings for source URL and gem name. Treat as malformed/untrusted illustrative content, not executable setup; no dependencies installed.
Travis example pins Ruby 2.3 and invokes bundle exec jekyll build; this historical runtime example is not a current safe recommendation, supported version audit or actual successful fixture.

Activating third-party CI can introduce integration, credential and cost effects requiring separate authority. All claims remain reference-only; no external service activated, source script executed, policy accepted or native publishing done.
